answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake in a marble-like public ledger before it may trade, so creating ten fake identities costs ten stakes instead of one. The stake sits in escrow while peers verify the agent's work; proven cheats forfeit it, while honest agents earn it back plus fees. A violet-flag reputation score then gates access to high-value jobs, and the escrow acts as a bridge between cheap identity creation and expensive trust: an attacker must risk capital per identity, which makes flooding the network unprofitable.
